summary: Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. A graduate student at the University of Chicago in 1991, she later served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Cornell University (~2000) and Professor at Harvard University.

Anne MacDonald works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida, Ashok Aklujkar, and others. Her posts include the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (Professor, 2010).

Anne Nishimura Morse specializes in Japanology, history, and archaeology. She studied under John M. Rosenfield, Taka Yanagisawa, and Yutaka Hirata. Her career includes visiting scholar appointments at Tokyo, Nara, and Kyoto national museums and a fellowship at Smith College.

Anne Ruth Hansen specializes in Buddhist, religious, and historical studies, having studied under Charles Hallisey. She held a post at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2007) before becoming Associate Professor (attested 2012) and Professor of History at UW–Madison (attested 2026).

Anne-Marie Blondeau is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied under Marcelle Lalou, Rolf Alfred Stein, Dagpo Rinpoche, and others. She was affiliated with the École Pratique des Hautes Études, including as an editorial consultant in 1982.

Anne-Marie Esnoul (1908–1996) was a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the EPHE under Sylvain Lévi and others, later serving as secretary-librarian at the Institut de Civilisation Indienne (1941–1966) and directeur d’études at the EPHE (1966–1977).
Annegret Bollée (1937–2021) was a linguist who pursued her studies at the University of Hamburg (~1957–1962), Aix-Marseille University, and the University of Bonn (1969).

Annelies Kammenhuber (1922–1995) specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. She studied under Ferdinand Sommer at Munich and Hamburg (Ph.D. 1950). She held professorships at the Pontifical Biblical Institute (1968) and the University of Munich (1964; 1969–1987).

Annemarie Schimmel (1922–2003) was a scholar of religious, Iranian/Central Asian, and Indological studies. She earned doctorates at Berlin and Marburg. Her main posts included Marburg, Ankara University, the University of Bonn, and Harvard University as professor of Indo-Muslim Culture (1967–1992).

Annemarie von Gabain (1901–1993) worked in Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (PhD 1930) and Peking University, she held posts at Ankara University, Berlin, and the University of Hamburg (1949–1966).

Annette Baier (1929–2012) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Otago and Somerville College, Oxford (PhD 1952). She held faculty posts at Carnegie Mellon University (~1968–1973) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1973–1995).

Annette L. Heitmann specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989) and the University of Vienna (doctoral degree, 2002), studying under Christian Lindtner and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Annette Schmiedchen is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin and completed her Habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~2004–2013), holding academic positions at both institutions.
Annette Susannah Beveridge (1842–1929) was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. She was educated at Bedford College, London between 1862 and 1867.

Annie Barber Clarke (1861–1956) was an Indology scholar who studied at Radcliffe College (1883–1886) under Charles Rockwell Lanman. She later worked as a teacher at Parsons School and Miss Brown's School.

Annie Montaut is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Paris Cité, and Paris Nanterre. She held posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University (1981–1987), Paris Nanterre (1987–1990), and INALCO (1990–2014).

Anshul Agarwal works in computational studies and Indology. He completed a Bachelor of Engineering at Vivekanand Education Society's Institute of Technology in 2014 and held a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur.

Antanas Poška (1903–1992) was a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at Vytautas Magnus University (1926–1929), the University of Mumbai (B.A. 1931–1933), and the University of Calcutta as a doctoral student (~1931–1936).

Anthony C. Yu (1938–2015) was a scholar of Sinology and religion. He studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. ~1963–1969), where he served on the faculty from ~1968 to 2005.

Anthony Cerulli specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Loyola University Chicago, Yale (M.A.), and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. 2007). He held posts at Hobart and William Smith Colleges (2008–2016) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2016–2021).
